description.narrative:
Goal: To support women and Girls in Armenia in driving the gender equality agenda forward in post-revolutionary and post-crisis situation for a more inclusive, equal, and democratic society
The overall goal will be achieved through three objectives:
Objective 1: Women CSOs create safe and empowering spaces for women and girls to heal, learn, and engage in democratic processes.
Objective 2: Develop and utilize an intersectional movement and gender equality agenda to engage with stakeholders.
Objective 3: Strengthen organizational capacities of Womens CSOs to address gender stereotypes, inequalities, GBV and WPS issues

WRC har lämnat in förslaget "Support for Resilient Women's Civil Society Organizing in the Context of Multiple Crises in Armenia" till Sida för programstöd. Den föreslagna projektperioden är 36 månader med en föreslagen budget på 1 200 000 Euro, vilket uppskattas till cirka 12 000 000 SEK. Programmets förväntade resultat är: - Att stärka kvinnor i riktade områden/samhällen som drabbats av konflikten för att påverka beslutsfattande på lokal nivå. - Att öka civilsamhällets förmåga att bidra till en gendersensitiv Covid-19 återhämtning. - Att stärka den inter-sektionella medborgarrörelsen (civila samhället och aktivister) för att driva fram en effektiv policyrespons mot könsbaserat våld och agendan för kvinnor fred- och säkerhet.

WRC has submitted "Support for Resilient Women's Civil Society Organizing in the Context of Multiple Crises in Armenia" proposal to Sida for the programme support. The proposed duration of the project is 36 months with requested budget of 1 200 000 Euro, which is estimated to about 12 000 000 SEK. The outcomes of the programme are: - To empower women in the local communities affected by the conflict to influence at the local development. - To increase the capacities of CSOs to advocate for gender sensitive COVID-19 recovery. - To strengthen intersectional civic movement (CSOs and activists) to drive an effective policy response to Gender based Violence and Women Peace and Security Agendas.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
The program enabled partner organizations to deliver concrete support services to women affected by GBV, including psychosocial counselling, legal assistance, and crisis response, resulting in increased access to multi-layered support for survivors. Sub-grants allowed CSOs to implement targeted projects in Yerevan and several regions, extending services to women who previously had limited or no access, including displaced women.
Economic empowerment activities provided practical results, with women participating in vocational trainings and small-scale income-generation initiatives, contributing to improved livelihoods and increased self-reliance among beneficiaries.
Advocacy efforts resulted in coordinated campaigns and joint actions by women's rights organizations, increasing visibility of GBV and WPS issues and contributing to their continued presence in public and policy discussions. Collaboration within coalitions strengthened collective positioning and messaging.
Showcase results
Adoption of the state strategy on Gender Equality (20252028): In 2025, amid shrinking civic space and increasing politicization of gender equality issues ahead of the 2026 parliamentary elections, the Armenian Government considered not adopting a standalone Gender Equality Strategy. Instead, the Government considered integrating gender equality objectives into other strategies and policy frameworks, a move that risked weakening visibility, accountability, and coordinated implementation of gender equality commitments. Through rapid coordination, the Women's Resource Center (WRC) mobilized 26 women's and human rights organizations to issue a joint statement to the Prime Minister advocating for adoption of a standalone strategy. Within one month, the Government adopted the State Gender Equality Strategy 20252028 and its Action Plan. The adoption preserved a dedicated national policy framework for gender equality, strengthened civil society's credibility in influencing high-level decision-making, and demonstrated that coordinated feminist advocacy can prevent policy regression even in a politically sensitive environment.
Ratification of ILO Convention No. 190 on Violence and Harassment in the World of Work: Gender-based violence and harassment in workplaces remained under-addressed in Armenia, with weak monitoring mechanisms and limited legal protection, particularly affecting women in vulnerable and informal employment. WRC and the Network of Women Labor Rights (11 CSOs) organized roundtables with Members of Parliament, Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs, and Health and Labor Inspection Body, and provided policy input to strengthen gender-sensitive labor reforms. In September 2025, Armenia ratified ILO Convention No. 190. Ratification aligned Armenian labor legislation with international standards, strengthened institutional responsibility for preventing workplace violence and harassment, and marked a structural step toward safer and more equitable working conditions for women.
Feminist safe space as infrastructure for civic resilience: Following mass displacement from Nagorno-Karabakh and during a pre-election period marked by anti-gender backlash and disinformation, women activists and human rights defenders faced burnout, trauma, and increased risks. WRCs Feminist safe space recorded over 1,000 visits in 2025 and mobilized 1,398 participants through empowerment programs, discussions, and activism. Trauma-informed services included 174 hours of individual psychological counseling, three group therapy cycles (30 women), and 240 legal hotline consultations. A retreat supported 15 Women Human Rights Defenders. Women reported increased resilience, reduced isolation, and strengthened leadership confidence. The Feminist safe space evolved into a sustainable civic resilience hub that enables continued engagement in advocacy and democratic participation despite shrinking civic space.
Coordinated civil society advocacy on GBV and WPS: Fragmented advocacy and rising pre-election polarization risked weakening gender equality priorities within national policy processes, including the WPS Action Plan and labor and demographic reforms. WRC facilitated consultations involving 25 women's organizations and 10 human rights organizations, strengthened joint advocacy mechanisms, and submitted gender-sensitive recommendations to five strategic policy documents. CSOs conducted five formal advocacy engagements with decision-makers. Collective efforts contributed to adoption of the Gender Equality Strategy and strengthened debate around WPS and labor reforms. Women's CSOs shifted from isolated actions to coordinated, evidence-based advocacy, increasing their legitimacy and influence in national policy processes. The strengthened network improved preparedness to safeguard women's rights during the 2026 pre-election period and reinforced long-term movement resilience.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
